## The problem

Our team of twelve has been running long-lived feature branches for over a year, and the seams are showing. Branches routinely live two to four weeks before merging, and merge day has become a dreaded ritual: conflicts span dozens of files, integration bugs surface only after the fact, and we lose a full day or more untangling divergent assumptions between branches that were developed in isolation. Because integration is deferred, we discover incompatibilities late, when they are most expensive to fix. Release velocity has slowed, and two of our last three releases slipped from last-minute merge fallout.

## The proposal

I propose we move to trunk-based development: all engineers commit small, frequent changes directly to main, gated by feature flags for anything incomplete, with a mandatory CI suite blocking any commit that breaks the build.

- Cap in-progress work at under one day of changes per commit, merged to main at least once daily
- Wrap unfinished features behind flags so main is always releasable
- Require green CI (tests plus linting) before any merge lands
- Pair this with a two-week trial period, measured against merge-conflict time and defect escape rate

This shrinks the integration gap from weeks to hours, surfaces conflicts while context is still fresh, and lets us release from main anytime.

## What could go wrong

The strongest objection is real: trunk-based development assumes a testing and CI culture we do not fully have yet. If our test suite has gaps, broken code reaches main faster and more often, and feature flags left untended will accumulate into technical debt that is worse than the branch clutter we started with. This is not a small risk — a team with flaky or slow CI can make trunk-based development actively more chaotic than what we have now, not less. I don't think we should dismiss this: it means our rollout has to start with hardening CI and flag hygiene before we lean on the practice, not after.

- Some engineers will need to unlearn habits built around isolated, long review branches, which will cost a few weeks of friction

I would like a decision by the end of next week.
